cards.text: Come on in, friend! This one's a song from the sons of Korah, a family of Levites who praised the LORD (2 Chronicles 20:19), and it opens with God founding a whole CITY. God gave me a planet the size of one bakery and I STILL can't keep the flour off the floor.

cards.question: The sons of Korah open their song with God's city. Where has He founded it?

cards.text: Turns out this city has a name: Zion. And the LORD doesn't just like her gates, friend. He LOVES them.

cards.question: True or false: The LORD loves the gates of Zion less than all the dwellings of Jacob.

cards.text: Then the song stops talking ABOUT the city and starts talking TO her, like she's right there in the room. Hey, I talk to my oven every morning, so no judgment here.

cards.question: The song speaks straight to the city the LORD loves. Fill it in: ___ things are ascribed to you, O city of God.

cards.text: Then the voice changes. God speaks, and He starts naming names: Rahab and Babylon, along with Philistia, Tyre and Cush.

cards.question: True or false: God mentions Rahab and Babylon, Philistia, Tyre and Cush among those who know Him.

cards.text: Wait. WAIT. Babylon? PHILISTIA? Friend, none of these are Israel, and I promise you, God is not done talking about them.

cards.question: God mentions these nations from outside Israel among those who know Him. What does He say when He mentions them?

answers.text: This one was born in Zion
This one is a stranger here

cards.question: It will be said of Zion that this one and that one were born in her. Who will establish Zion?

cards.text: Then the LORD makes it official and writes it down. Friend, what the LORD writes does NOT end up lost in the back of a junk drawer, and trust me, I checked every corner of that thing.

cards.question: The LORD writes down that this one was born in Zion. Fill it in: The LORD will record in the ___ of the peoples.

cards.text: One more line, friend. And this song doesn't fade out quiet, it goes out with MUSIC.

cards.question: Psalm 87 ends with music. Who's making it?

cards.text: And they proclaim, “All my springs of joy are in You.” Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer getting my joy from rubber band stretching contests, so I can tell you these folks found the REAL spring.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card has three sentences: the city is named, the LORD's love is introduced, and then emphasized in a separate sentence. Non-opening story cards are limited to one or two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This non-opening story card uses five separately punctuated statements or questions: "Wait.", "WAIT.", "Babylon?", "PHILISTIA?", and the closing sentence. That exceeds the one-to-two-sentence limit.
